Aaron / Acme team —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a compact design and an acceptance checklist we think will address procurement and SOC reviewers: telemetry-egress-design-v1.pdf. High-level decisions and responsibilities below:

1) Transport and endpoints
   - Preferred: Splunk HEC over HTTPS (443) using mutual TLS where the customer can present certs. HEC supports per-source tokens; we recommend MTLS+HEC token for high assurance.
   - Alternative: Syslog TLS (RFC 5425) to a customer-managed forwarder for customers who require syslog.

2) Authentication and rotation
   - HEC tokens: support rolling tokens; Redwood will accept a new token via an API call and drain connections before revocation. Documented rotation window: 24h overlap.
   - MTLS certs: support standard CA-signed certs (customer-provided) or mutual TLS with Redwood-managed client certs. We recommend customer-managed server certs for direct HEC.

3) Evidence & compliance artifacts
   - TLS cipher suite, connection logs (source IPs, cert thumbprints), HEC token issuance/rotation events, and delivery ACKs.
   - We can produce an "egress audit bundle" covering a 30-day window (delivery logs + checksums).

4) Data handling controls
   - Configurable message-level redaction (PII masks) before egress, configurable retention policy for cached payloads.
   - At-rest: temporary encryption for short-term KV caches; long-term storage uses KMS-backed encryption.

5) Offline / restricted egress patterns
   - If Acme disallows direct outbound to Splunk: recommended pattern is an encrypted, customer-controlled S3 bucket where Redwood writes encrypted batches (SSE-KMS) and an Acme forwarder pulls to Splunk.

Checklist items for procurement (short):
   - Confirm endpoint type: HEC (HTTPS) or Syslog/TLS
   - Confirm auth model: MTLS+HEC token or token-only
   - Required retention windows for delivery attempts and cached telemetry
   - Required redaction rules and accepted formats
   - Evidence package scope and frequency

Attachments: [Attachment: telemetry-egress-design-v1.pdf (pdf)]

Next steps: Kimberly — can you validate the KMS / evidence wording and add language for HSM-backed key attestations? Marissa — can you add the expected payload schema for traces/metrics/logs and sample ingestion mapping to Splunk?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Diego — quick internal addendum before we send back to Atlas/Acme:

- Cert rotation / lifetime: propose default rotation = 90 days with an automated renewal workflow. For customers requiring FIPS/HSM attestations, we will call out HSM-backed key origin and provide a cert thumbprint history.
- Token policy: require token rotation every 30 days for HEC tokens; we will provide tooling and an API contract for token replace-with-grace-period (24h overlap as Diego noted).
- Evidence package: create an evidence_manifest_v1.zip that contains: TLS negotiation logs (metadata only), delivery ACKs (per-batch), KMS key id + last-rotate timestamp (no private key material).
- Retention/backup: temporary caches will be set to 7 days by default unless Acme requests otherwise; if we stage to S3, it will be SSE-KMS with bucket policies limiting access to Acme principals.
- Network egress control: all outbound egress will be proxied through a customer-configurable NAT/egress IP allowlist with TCP 443 only. We should include a sample iptables/ip rule snippet for our ops runbook.

Attached: [Attachment: evidence_manifest_v1.zip (zip)]

Marissa — can you prepare a short JSON payload sample (index/time/level/message + trace_id + service) and a Splunk HEC props stanza we can paste into the procurement packet?

Kimberly Park
Director, Security Integrations, Redwood Inference
